verdict.rationale: Sketch is a design tool, not an agent, so an official MCP server story applies. First-party docs say Sketch ships a built-in MCP Server that lets AI clients like ChatGPT or Claude interact directly with Sketch, and the AI page says any MCP-compatible client can connect at no extra cost. The server is local-only and the evidence is vendor-only. Missing for 10: documented tool/capability list and setup depth in the evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration, and any remote or hosted endpoint option beyond local-only.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Sketch includes a built-in MCP Server, a lightweight local-only web server that lets AI clients like ChatGPT or Claude interact directly with Sketch.
Connect any MCP-compatible AI client you like to Sketch. There are no tokens to buy, no extra tiers, and no add-ons.
Point your AI client at a repo to recreate text styles, colors, UI components, and even entire pages inside Sketch.
